candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classifies this binary as malware with probability 0.93, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking, with none pulling the other way. Contributions are spread fairly evenly (+0.0053 to +0.0103), so no single artifact drives the call. Many of the n-grams are the bit-rotation and carry-chain arithmetic typical of hashing and cipher inner loops. Rotation patterns include MOV ROL (+0.009936), ROR ROL (+0.006144), ROL ROR (+0.005670), ROL MOV (+0.005566) and XOR ROL (+0.005386). Multi-precision carry/borrow patterns include SUB SBB (+0.010277, the top feature), MOV ADC (+0.006873), XOR ADC (+0.006674), SUB ADC (+0.006659) and ADC SUB (+0.006042). Together these resemble the mixing and modular-arithmetic steps of proof-of-work hash routines. The remaining features (SUB PUSH, MOVZX PUSH, ADD PUSH, CMP PUSH, POP TEST, ADD OR, ADD POP) look like stack and register-handling glue around such routines, and they add moderate positive weight. Three features (CALL ADD, CMOVZ MOV, TEST JS) have a reported frequency of 0.000000 yet carry positive SHAP, so the model is using their absence or near-absence as a signal. That is statistical rather than behavioral evidence. The evidence has two limits. No function-level locations, API calls or strings were provided, so the code cannot be tied to a specific mining algorithm or to network and pool behavior. Rotate and add-with-carry sequences also occur in legitimate cryptographic libraries. The tier therefore rests on the high model probability and the coherent cluster of hash-like arithmetic n-grams, not on direct proof of mining.
